alex: Quick heads-up — starting POC with Pinnacle today. They want Redwood Private in their VPC, BYOK with HSM-backed keys, and a cert rotation plan. Can we get a minimal checklist for what they need to provide (CSRs / KMS policies / IP allowlist)?

sam: Yep. High-level checklist: 
- customer CSR (PEM) for control-plane TLS cert or CA chain if they want to sign
- KMS details: provider (AWS/Azure/GCP), whether CMK is importable or CloudHSM is available
- public key material or wrapped key for BYOK import (never plain private keys)
- CIDR ranges to allow for control plane + data plane 
- SAML provider metadata (if they want SSO)
- point person for cert/key exchange and slack/email for secure transfer

maria: Adding infra items:
- preferred region + VPC subnet IDs and NAT/IGW details
- bastion / jump host IPs for initial bootstrap (we create ephemeral admin user)
- secrets mounting preference (we support AWS KMS/Azure KeyVault/GCP KMS and HSM appliances via PKCS#11 bridge)

jordan: Can we use our existing AWS KMS CMK? Security mandates HSM-backed key and rotation every 90 days. Also need audit logs for key usage (who/when).

sam: Short answer: yes, with caveats. Options: 
1) Use AWS KMS (Customer Managed CMK): we integrate with their CMK via IAM role. No key extraction. We use envelope encryption — Redwood holds a data-encryption key encrypted by their CMK. Audit via CloudTrail.
2) Use AWS CloudHSM / on-prem HSM: we can integrate via PKCS#11 for signing/wrapping operations if they want to keep key material entirely in HSM. This is the true BYOK path.

If they want to import an existing key (move private key into our control plane), we only accept wrapped key material using our key-import tool and a short-lived import token (we never accept raw PEM private keys over email).

security-reviewer: From compliance side, we'll need:
- key policy sample for CMK (allow Redwood role with kms:Decrypt kms:GenerateDataKey)
- rotation SLA (we support automated rotation or customer-initiated)
- proof of HSM-backed protection (CloudHSM attestation or HSM vendor certs)

sam: Example AWS CMK policy snippet (customer to attach to CMK):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodRole",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-poc-role"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey", "kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```
(we'll provide the exact role ARN once we spin up the POC)

maria: For certs we usually do this flow:
1) Customer generates a keypair locally and creates a CSR: `openssl req -new -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -keyout private.key -out request.csr`
2) Customer uploads CSR to us over our secure upload link (we'll provide)
3) We sign & return a PEM cert chain or they provide a CA chain to install

sam: If they prefer to have Redwood generate the private key, we can, but most enterprise customers insist on generating keys in-house or in their HSM.

jordan: How do we transfer the wrapped key to you? SFTP or a pre-signed S3? Security prefers ephemeral presigned S3 with MFA delete disabled for upload window.

sam: Presigned S3 with short TTL is fine. For HSM-wrapped key imports we also require the import token flow: we generate a short-lived import token and a public wrapping key; customer uses their on-prem tool to wrap the PKCS#8 blob and uploads it. We'll provide a step-by-step during onboarding.

alex: Can you write one-liner instructions I can send to their security team? Keep it copy-paste friendly.

sam: Sure — copy below.
"To onboard BYOK for Redwood Private: 1) Confirm KMS provider (AWS/Azure/GCP) and whether CMK is importable or HSM is available. 2) Generate key material in your HSM or KMS. For HSM import: request an import token from Redwood, wrap your PKCS#8 private key with the provided wrapping key, upload to pre-signed S3. For CMK integration: attach the provided Redwood IAM role to your CMK policy and enable CloudTrail logging. For control-plane TLS: generate CSR (`openssl req -new -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -keyout private.key -out request.csr`) and upload PEM CSR to Redwood secure upload link. 3) Provide VPC subnet IDs, allowed CIDRs, and SAML metadata if needed. 4) Expect an ephemeral admin user for initial bootstrap; rotate credentials after first login."

security-reviewer: Also ask them to provide a contact in their infra/sec team and a copy of their KMS key policy. We'll run it against our checklist.

devops-bot: Ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/POC-6789 — assigned to sam, maria.

alex: Great — Jordan, I'll drop this in an email and ping you a secure upload link. Tracking this on the POC board. Thanks team :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks — will collect CSR and the CMK policy, target to upload by EOD tomorrow.

sam: I'll prep the import-token flow docs and the exact role ARN once infra spins the pod.

maria: Scheduling bootstrap window Thurs 09:00 PT. Will send calendar invite once Jordan confirms IP allowlist.

alex: perfect. closing loop for now.
